''De FC'' ({{lit|The FC}}) | founded = {{start date and age|1971|6|16|df=y}} | ground = [[Euroborg]] | capacity = 22,550 | owner = FC Groningen Beheer [[B.V.]] | chairman = Jakob Klompien | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Dick Lukkien]] | league = {{Dutch football updater|Groningen}} | season = {{Dutch football updater|Groningen2}} | position = {{Dutch football updater|Groningen3}} | current = 2026–27 FC Groningen season | website = {{URL|https://www.fcgroningen.nl}} | pattern_la1 = _groningen2425h | pattern_b1 = _groningen2425h | pattern_ra1 = _groningen2425h | pattern_sh1 = _groningen2425h | pattern_so1 = | leftarm1 = FFFFFF | body1 = 000000 | rightarm1 = FFFFFF | shorts1 = FFFFFF | socks1 = FFFFFF | pattern_la2 = | pattern_b2 = | pattern_ra2 = | pattern_sh2 = | pattern_so2 = | leftarm2 = | body2 = | rightarm2 = | shorts2 = | socks2 = | pattern_la3 = | pattern_b3 = | pattern_ra3 = | pattern_sh3 = | pattern_so3 = | leftarm3 = | body3 = | rightarm3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = }} '''Football Club Groningen''' ({{IPA|nl|ɛfˈseː ˈɣroːnɪŋə(n)}}) is a Dutch professional [[association football]] club based in [[Groningen]]. Founded in 1971 as the successor of [[GVAV-Rapiditas|GVAV]], Groningen compete in the [[Eredivisie]], the first tier of [[Football in the Netherlands|Dutch football]]. Groningen played in the Eredivisie during their first three seasons, before the side were [[Promotion and relegation|relegated]] to the [[Eerste Divisie]] in [[1973–74 Eredivisie|1973–74]] as they got into financial difficulties. Groningen were [[Promotion and relegation|promoted]] back to the Eredivisie as champions in [[1979–80 Eerste Divisie|1979–80]] with a squad composed mostly of players who were recruited from the club's youth academy, and remained in the top flight for 18 seasons before they dropped to the second tier in [[1997–98 Eredivisie|1997–98]]. The team won promotion back to the Eredivisie in [[1999–2000 Eerste Divisie|1999–2000]], where they remained for 23 seasons before suffering relegation in [[2022–23 Eredivisie|2022–23]]. Groningen finished as runners-up in the [[2023–24 Eerste Divisie]] and returned to the Eredivisie at the first attempt. Groningen have won the [[KNVB Cup]] once, in [[2014–15 KNVB Cup|2014–15]], and were runners-up in [[1988–89 KNVB Cup|1988–89]]. Groningen achieved their highest league finish in [[1990–91 Eredivisie|1990–91]] when they ranked third in the Eredivisie, competing for the league title until the latter part of the season. The side have participated in [[UEFA competitions|European competitions]] on several occasions; Groningen's [[FC Groningen in European football|first participation in European competition]] came during the [[1983–84 UEFA Cup]], when they defeated [[Atlético Madrid]] on [[Two-legged tie|aggregate]] in the first round, but were eliminated by [[Inter Milan]] in the following round. [[Erwin Koeman]], [[Ronald Koeman]], [[Arjen Robben]] and [[Virgil van Dijk]] started their careers at Groningen, while it was [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]]'s first European club. The team's first home ground was [[Stadion Oosterpark|Oosterparkstadion]]; since 2006, they have played their home games at [[Euroborg]]. Groningen's home [[Kit (association football)|kit]] colours are based on the city's coat of arms: green and white. The club is nicknamed "Trots van het Noorden" ({{lit|Pride of the North}}), and has a rivalry with [[Friesland|Frisian]] side [[SC Heerenveen|Heerenveen]], with whom it contests the [[Derby of the North|Derby van het Noorden]] ({{lit|Derby of the North}})."}}
